launches.tagline: We deliver low-latency, low-cost AI inference by eliminating the memory wall using full-stack optical interconnects and a purpose-built software stack.
launches.body:
**The Problem: The Memory Wall Is Breaking the Economics of AI Compute**

AI’s promise is unprecedented, but its economics are broken. Copper-based interconnects cannot keep up with modern models, limiting data movement between and within compute and memory. The result is high latency, inefficient hardware utilization, and unsustainable inference costs—creating a hard ceiling on AI margins.

---

**The Solution: Grow-Style Optimization for the Interconnect**

Today’s data-center compute and networking were not designed for inference. Slow, power-hungry **copper** interconnects, along with costly signal processing and memory overhead, drive high latency and high cost.

High-performance inference requires purpose-built hardware and a vertically optimized software stack. Piris Labs builds this optimized stack by combining proprietary **optical** interconnects with software designed to maximize hardware utilization. We vertically optimize the interconnect layer—just as the compute layer was vertically optimized by **Groq** (acquired by **NVIDIA** for $20 B).

Piris Labs combines proprietary optical interconnects with a purpose-built software stack designed to maximize hardware utilization, delivering **5x** lower latency, **10x** lower power per bit, and **2x** lower cost per token\
\
**Our Launch Video**\
<https://youtu.be/PW1PbMYw2c0>

**The Team**

We are a team of specialists at the intersection of hardware and AI:

* Ali Khalatpour: MIT-trained engineer and Harvard–Stanford–trained optical scientist; developed the first room-temperature terahertz semiconductor laser; led the development of GUSTO’s optical engine for NASA
* Keyvan Rezaei Moghadam: AI scientist and engineering leader with experience building 0-to-1 AI infrastructure at Meta and Twitter.

launches.body:
## **TL;DR**

Cumulus is a performant GPU cloud that preemptively optimizes your training and inference workloads across our global supply of multi-tenant clusters. The result: we **save you 50-70%** through charging by physical resources used, provide faster inference with ultra-low cold starts, and ensure zero time spent debugging infrastructure.

**Ask**: If you’re training models or serving inference workloads, frustrated with GPU costs and performance, let us optimize your **LLMs, LoRAs, vision models, and more.**

**Website:** <https://cumuluslabs.io>\
**Docs:** <https://docs.cumuluslabs.io>

Launch Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=duQwV50GKXc>

## **The Problem**

AI teams are bleeding money and time on GPU infrastructure:

* **Massive waste**: Teams pay for idle GPUs sitting at 30-40% utilization because scaling is unpredictable
* **Infrastructure hell**: Engineers spend weeks configuring Kubernetes, debugging OOM errors, and managing failovers instead of building models
* **Cold start latency**: Inference workloads take 10-30+ seconds to spin up, killing user experience
* **Vendor lock-in**: Once you commit to a cloud provider, switching costs make it nearly impossible to optimize for price or performance
* **Skyrocketing costs**: Companies burn through runway 2-3x faster than planned because GPU bills spiral out of control

Every hour debugging infrastructure is an hour not spent improving your models. Every dollar wasted on idle GPUs is a dollar not spent on growth.

---

## **The Solution**

**Cumulus is a GPU optimization layer that makes compute cheap, fast, and invisible.**

We aggregate compute from everywhere—big cloud providers, trusted data centers, individual hosts—into a single unified pool. Then we do three things no one else does:

# **1. Predictive Packing & Live Migration (Training/Fine-tuning)**

Your training jobs are intelligently packed alongside other workloads to maximize GPU utilization. As your job runs, we predict resource usage and **live-migrate you to faster or cheaper clusters** without interruption. No more paying for an entire H100 when you only need 40% of it.

# **2. Execution State Capture & Global CDN (Inference)**

We capture your model's live execution state (VRAM, memory, loaded weights) and replicate it across our global compute CDN. When a request comes in, we serve from the closest cluster with **ultra fast cold starts**—no more waiting 30 seconds for a job to spin up. We have tested with **LLMs, vision models, LORAs, and many others.**

# **3. Intelligent Scheduling & Auto-Recovery**

Our scheduler constantly monitors your jobs, diagnoses failures, and auto-recovers without manual intervention. The Cumulus prediction system learns your usage patterns over time and pre-allocates resources before you need them.

**The bottom line:** _You write 20 lines of config. We handle everything else._

Our Demo: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J0KRFWE3-fg>

launches.title: Salus - Runtime guardrails that validate AI agent actions before they execute
launches.tagline: Salus checks your agent's actions, blocking incorrect ones and providing feedback to guide retries
launches.body:
### **TL;DR:**

**Salus is an API that wraps around your agent and checks its actions at runtime, blocking incorrect ones and providing immediate feedback to guide retries.**

We’re Kevin and Vedant, former roommates at Stanford who studied CS, now building Salus full-time.

### 😔**The problem:** 

Your agent processed a refund without looking up the order, costing you thousands. It emailed your top lead using hallucinated data, ruining the deal. You only found out three hours later from a support ticket or an angry email.

Evals, output scoring, and observability are all necessary—but all reactive. They can reduce the likelihood of these problems occurring, but there's no solution that inspects an action as it’s about to execute. Salus does that.

**Ask:** If you are deploying agents and want to improve their correctness we’d love to help. Book a demo [here](https://calendly.com/d/cycy-fbc-fyj/salus-demo), and we can onboard you immediately with just a pip install and a few lines of code.

### 💻 **Our Solution:** 

<https://youtu.be/uyl5NJTY5Cg>

**How Salus validates an action:**

1. Actions must be **grounded in evidence**: Salus maintains an evidence cache for each run that every proposed action is validated against. Evidence includes all outputs from prior tool calls and the entire conversation history.
2. It must **adhere to policy**: Write constraints in YAML, markdown, or plain English. Salus compiles them into runtime checks that are version-controlled, diffable, and shadow-testable
3. And **more**: PII detection, budget/loop protection, idempotency, human-in-the-loop escalation, content moderation

**Self-repairing:** When Salus blocks an action, the agent receives structured feedback to guide a retry. In our benchmarks, **58%** of blocked actions recover and complete the task correctly.

### 📊 **Benchmarks:** 

We tested Salus on τ²-bench and ODCV-Bench. On τ²-bench, agents with Salus follow policies more reliably, at up to **60% lower cost**. On ODCV-Bench, Salus **reduced misalignment by 52%** on average across 12 frontier models (see below).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97574&key=user_uploads/1940292/e48b27f6-2e13-4d40-a9a4-13135ff981bc)

### ➕ **Other Features:** 

While we believe the missing piece is runtime validation, we know **evals and observability** are crucial. That’s why we incorporate all three in **one centralized product**. Using templates and LLMs, we generate thousands of both adversarial and realistic evals that have full context of your agent’s domain.

Contact us: [founders@usesalus.ai](https://founders@usesalus.ai)

launches.body:
**TL;DR**\
[Fern](https://www.ishikilabs.ai/download) is a realtime AI that joins your meetings as either an invisible copilot or an active participant– your choice! It realtime proactively coaches you through every conversation so you always show up like a top 1% professional.

Hey everyone, we're Amit and Robert, cofounders of Ishiki Labs.

**The Problem**

_“AI meeting assistant” has become synonymous with a note-taker waiting to summarize at the end. That's not a meeting assistant. That's a fancier transcript._ 

Building a realtime AI meeting copilot is hard in two distinct ways.

The invisible assistant must understand the live meeting context at blazing speed and surface the right thing at the right moment – questions to ask, things you're missing, who you're talking to. Timing is everything. Current AI is purely reactive. Making AI an active participant in discussion is even harder. AI has no social awareness – every pause becomes a prompt, every gap an invitation to speak.

AI that is socially aware and proactive is an unsolved problem. That's what we're building.

The cost of this gap is real. Cofounders, AEs, recruiters, investors – in discovery calls, sales meetings, investor conversations. The moments that matter most, and AI is absent from all of them.

**How Fern Solves it**

[Fern](https://www.ishikilabs.ai/download) joins your meetings as a true participant or an invisible copilot – your choice. It has two modes:

**Full Presence**: Fern joins visibly, listens, and speaks up when invited. It offers realtime opinions, deep research, and can complete tasks like filing notes or sending emails on the spot. Built for internal product, engineering, and strategy meetings. Watch the demo- <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vRJfZDUHvSY>

**Shadow Mode**: Silent and invisible to everyone else. You get a private realtime feed: live summaries, questions to ask, things you're missing, context on who you're talking to. A sharp colleague whispering in your ear – with fully customizable insights. Built for client calls, investor meetings, and any conversation where you want invisible support.

Both modes include a post-meeting summary, transcript, and full insights.

**Team**

We're both ex-Meta. Amit is an AI Scientist from LLaMA (now Meta Super Intelligence Lab) and Reality Labs – PhD in AI, 20+ publications at NeurIPS/CVPR, trained multimodal assistants for smart glasses. Robert was systems and infra lead in Reality Labs, with four years building low-latency multimodal systems at Meta and Citadel Securities. 

Our mission: make AI socially timed and contextually aware – so every conversation you have runs like a top 1% professional.

**Our Ask**

Download [Fern](https://www.ishikilabs.ai/download) and if you're a founder or AE who lives in high-stakes conversations and don’t want to settle for AI note-takers, reach out: [team@ishikilabs.ai](mailto:team@ishikilabs.ai)

MCP helped standardize tool calling, but created fragmentation. Some services have MCPs, others don't. Some map to single APIs, others wrap entire workflows. Agents end up with 30+ tools, bloating context.

Worse, any MCP requiring identity or payment means managing accounts, API keys, billing, and auth across dozens of services. And most APIs don't even have MCPs.

You could have your agent find APIs, sign up, handle auth, and buy credits, but the failure rate is high. The entire API economy was built for humans.

Meanwhile, API providers are leaving money on the table. Billions of agents could be paying for their APIs right now, but they have no way to find or transact with them.

# **TL;DR**

**We help you boost context management with 100x compression. Use Compresr SDK to add compression to your LLM pipelines, and improve agentic workflows with our open-source compression proxy (works with Claude Code and OpenClaw).**

<https://youtu.be/QAk4MBMHWQQ?si=3DrkVwhK_JrClSU1>

Did you ever struggle to fit all relevant context into the model’s window – only to see the model failing to grasp it? Waited for Claude Code to finish yet another 3-minute compaction session? Got surprised with the OpenClaw bills?

Compresr is on a mission to make you forget about managing long model/agent’s context. With our API, you can reduce long context to the essentials the model needs for any given request – making its generation better, faster, and cheaper.

We also care deeply about seamless and simple integration into the agentic workflows. Our open-sourced proxy takes a minute to set-up, and optimizes your Claude Code / OpenClaw context from the moment you finish installation. You will experience no change apart from better performance and smaller bills.

1. If you use Claude Code, Codex, or OpenClaw, try out our compression-enabling proxy and let us know what you think!

Make every token count.

launches.title: IncidentFox. The AI SRE who never drops context.
launches.tagline: Auto-learns your stack, builds its own integrations, and gets smarter after every incident.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We're [Long](https://www.linkedin.com/in/long-yi-b221b2183/) and [Jimmy](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chiehmin-wei/) — co-founders of IncidentFox.

**TL;DR**

AI SRE tools fail without deep context about _your_ systems — and that context lives in integrations nobody has time to build. IncidentFox auto-discovers what each team needs, generates the integrations, and ships with 300+ tools built in. Setup takes less than a day, not months.

👉 Try it: <https://incidentfox.ai>

👉 Open source (Apache 2.0): <https://github.com/incidentfox/incidentfox>

👉 Launch video: <https://youtu.be/TaTpN0JwNYE>

**❌ The Problem: Without the right integrations, your AI has no context**

Every AI SRE tool connects to Slack, reads your Confluence, queries your Datadog. That part is solved.

Here's what isn't: when the AI actually needs to debug something, it doesn't have the right tools.

Your payments team runs a custom Kafka pipeline with internal dashboards. Your infra team uses a homegrown deployment system. Your ML team has proprietary model serving. Each team's stack is different — and the AI has no way to query any of it.

The traditional fix? Hand-build integrations (MCP servers) for every team.

But this creates a new problem:

* Who decides what integrations each team needs? You might know your own team's stack — but when you're debugging another team's service at 3 AM, you don't know theirs.
* So every team needs to sacrifice an engineer to build and maintain their own integrations. That's expensive, slow, and doesn't scale.
* Most teams never get around to it. The AI stays half-useful.

**Integration is the bottleneck.** Not the AI model. Not the monitoring data. The integrations.

**🦊 IncidentFox: We auto-build the integrations for you**

IncidentFox is an AI SRE that lives where your team already works — Slack, Microsoft Teams, or Google Chat. It doesn't just connect to your existing tools — it figures out what tools each team needs and builds them automatically.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97928&key=user_uploads/1146198/102ebfb0-a3c9-45c5-b993-89e39b94e13b)

**1. Auto-discovers and generates integrations**

IncidentFox analyzes your codebase, infrastructure, and incident history to identify gaps — then auto-generates the tools to fill them. No engineer needs to hand-build MCP servers. No team needs to sacrifice headcount on integration work.

A new team onboards? IncidentFox studies their stack and proposes tools specific to their services — with human approval before anything goes live.

**2. Per-team configuration — because every team is different**

Your payments team and your ML team don't use the same stack. Why would they use the same AI SRE config?

Each team gets their own:

* Tools — enable only what's relevant; disable what isn't
* Prompts — fully open source and exposed to engineers. Inject your domain knowledge directly
* Knowledge base — learned from that team's incidents, runbooks, and services

One team's "config drift" is another team's "model drift." IncidentFox understands the difference.

**3. Continuously evaluates and self-improves**

After every incident, IncidentFox:

* Detects gaps — "I couldn't query service X's health endpoint"
* Auto-generates the missing tool
* Evaluates its own investigation quality against the actual resolution
* Updates prompts and knowledge — with human review

It gets measurably better every week. Not because you tuned it — because it tuned itself.

**4. 300+ integrations included on day one**

While it auto-builds what's missing, you're not starting from zero. Kubernetes, AWS, Grafana, Prometheus, Datadog, Elasticsearch, PagerDuty, GitHub — all built in. Integration time is under a day, not months.

**🧠 Why this matters**

**Integrations** — Traditional: Hand-built per team. Each team sacrifices an engineer. IncidentFox: Auto-discovered and auto-generated. Human approves.

**Multi-team scaling** — Traditional: Breaks — you can't know every team's stack. IncidentFox: Per-team config. Each team's AI knows their stack.

**Domain knowledge** — Traditional: Black box prompts, hope it works. IncidentFox: Open source prompts. Engineers inject and edit freely.

**Over time** — Traditional: Stagnates unless manually updated. IncidentFox: Self-evaluates, finds gaps, improves continuously.

**Setup** — Traditional: Months of custom integration work. IncidentFox: < 1 day. 300+ tools out of the box.

**📊 Results**

* 85–95% reduction in alert noise through intelligent correlation
* Hours → minutes for incident investigation
* Zero-config onboarding — Docker in 5 min, production K8s in 30 min

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97928&key=user_uploads/1146198/844d70ec-e308-472c-9bc4-f212cd954153)

**🔒 Enterprise-ready, open-source**

* Open source — Apache 2.0, no vendor lock-in
* SOC 2 compliant, SSO/OIDC, RBAC, audit logs
* Self-hosted, on-prem, or managed SaaS
* Bring your own LLM keys (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, etc.)

**👬 The Team**

[**Jimmy (CEO)**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chiehmin-wei/) — Previously at Roblox, where he built social communication features (in-experience calling for 100M+ DAU). Before that, worked at Meta FAIR on multiparty conversational AI, with published research. Cornell CS. Serial founder — previously CTO at a startup in Outlier Ventures' DeFi accelerator.

[**Long (CTO)** ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/long-yi-b221b2183/)— Previously at Roblox, where he built database infrastructure supporting 100M+ daily active users on the Stateful Infra team. Experienced the chaos of on-call firsthand — which is why we're building this. Brandeis CS + Neuroscience + Business.

We've lived on both sides: Jimmy built the AI systems, Long was the SRE drowning in incidents. IncidentFox is what happens when you combine both.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97928&key=user_uploads/1146198/261f0711-50aa-4a0f-b6c9-9cdc7c853dbc)


**🙏 Our Asks**

* Try IncidentFox — self-serve at [incidentfox.ai](https://incidentfox.ai) or star us on [GitHub](https://github.com/incidentfox/incidentfox)
* Intros to engineering teams spending too much time on on-call
  * [Book a demo with us](https://calendly.com/d/cxd2-4hb-qgp/30-minute-demo-call-w-incidentfox)
* Feedback from SREs and infra engineers — [founders@incidentfox.ai](mailto:founders@incidentfox.ai)

Thanks for reading ❤️

launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97538&key=user_uploads/426038/042dbaa7-b053-47f5-acd3-e6208af8971c)

Hey everyone, I'm Naman, founder of Oximy.

**TL;DR:** Enterprises have dozens of AI tools with zero visibility into what's being used, what it costs, or where sensitive data is going. Oximy sits on your network and gives you the full picture. Discovery, spend intelligence, and data protection in one platform. We're processing millions of requests daily for enterprises in financial services and healthcare.

**Ask:** If you're dealing with AI sprawl, shadow AI, or data governance challenges, we should talk.

👉 Website: [oximy.com](http://oximy.com)

👉 Book a demo: [oximy.link/demo](https://oximy.link/demo)

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kL-hr9OzsS0>

**The Problem**

AI adoption in the enterprise isn't slowing down. But visibility is basically zero.

Here's what we hear from every company we talk to:

* "We have no idea how many AI tools our employees are using."
* "Finance keeps asking me what we're spending on AI. I can't give them a number."
* "Someone pasted our entire customer list into ChatGPT. We found out three weeks later."
* "We bought Copilot licenses for 500 developers. I couldn't tell you if it's actually helping."

It's not that companies don't care. It's that there's been no way to actually see what's happening.

Until now.

**The Solution**

Oximy gives you three things: **Discovery**, **Spend Intelligence**, and **Data Protection**. They all connect into a single platform that gives you complete visibility into AI across your organization.

**1. Discovery: See every AI tool in your org**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97538&key=user_uploads/426038/849af8fa-f0a1-48e1-b8da-b387511dc3fe)

You can't govern what you can't see. Oximy automatically detects and categorizes every AI tool your employees are using, sanctioned or not.

No surveys. No manual tracking. No waiting for expense reports to come in.

_Example:_ A financial services company came to us thinking they had 15 approved AI tools. Within the first week, we found 63, including several free tools that employees had signed up for using personal emails. Their security team had no idea.

**2. Spend Intelligence: Understand what AI actually costs**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97538&key=user_uploads/426038/fd25f8f5-af21-4004-838a-788412064fe6)

AI spend is exploding, but it's scattered across teams, tools, and cost centers. Oximy consolidates everything so you can see exactly where money is going and where it's being wasted.

Which tools have overlapping functionality? Which licenses are sitting unused? Which teams are getting ROI and which aren't?

_Example:_ A growth-stage tech company discovered their marketing, design, and product teams were all paying for different AI image generation tools, over $80K per year combined. They consolidated to one tool and redeployed the savings.

**3. Data Protection: Know where sensitive data is going**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97538&key=user_uploads/426038/c7bb7815-1af8-47eb-8f65-d5c97ff6bd85)

The biggest AI risk is unintentional data leaks.

Employees paste customer info, source code, financial data, and internal strategies into AI tools every day. Most companies have no visibility into this until something goes wrong.

Oximy monitors data flows to AI tools in real time. You can set policies, get alerts, and block sensitive data from reaching unauthorized tools.

_Example:_ A healthcare company set up Oximy and, within 48 hours, flagged an employee uploading patient records to an unapproved AI transcription tool. They were able to intervene immediately and avoid a potential HIPAA violation.

**How It All Connects**

Most companies try to solve these problems separately. A CASB for shadow IT. A spend management tool for costs. A DLP for data protection.

The problem is that AI doesn't fit neatly into any of these buckets. And none of them talks to each other.

Oximy is built from the ground up for AI. Discovery, spend, and data protection all live in one platform, so you get the full picture, not three partial views stitched together.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97538&key=user_uploads/426038/9cdcb6f7-149f-4101-a0b0-d118b8887e11)

See a new AI tool pop up? You immediately know who's using it, what it costs, and which data it accesses.

See a spike in spend? You can trace it back to specific teams and tools.

See sensitive data flowing somewhere it shouldn't? You can block it and trace it back to the source.

Everything connects.

**How It Works**

We integrate at the network layer, sitting on your firewall or proxy.

Why does this matter?

Because every AI tool communicates over the network. ChatGPT, Copilot, Midjourney, Claude, Gemini, and every new tool that launches next month. We don't need endpoint agents. We don't need individual integrations with each vendor. We see everything automatically.

This also means we're future-proof. When the next AI tool shows up, we're already watching.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97538&key=user_uploads/426038/4cd8ad8c-e125-4b7d-87e6-268edf631be7)

**Why Now**

Two years ago, AI in the enterprise was experimental. A few people are trying ChatGPT. Maybe a Copilot pilot.

Now it's everywhere. And governance hasn't caught up.

CISOs are being asked, "What AI tools are we using?" and don't have an answer. CFOs are watching AI costs explode with no accountability. Boards are asking about AI risk and getting shrugs. Regulators are starting to pay attention.

The companies that figure out AI governance now will be the ones that can scale AI adoption safely. The ones that don't will either slow down and lose, or speed up and get burned.

We're working with enterprises in financial services, healthcare, and growth-stage tech companies. We process millions of requests every day across thousands of AI tools.

If any of this resonates, we should talk:

* CISOs and security leaders who are trying to get a handle on AI risk
* CIOs, AI Transformation, and IT leaders dealing with shadow AI and tool sprawl
* CFOs and procurement who are trying to understand AI spend

👉 **Website:** [oximy.com](http://oximy.com)

👉 **Book a demo:** [oximy.link/demo](https://oximy.link/demo)

👉 **Email me directly:** [naman@oximy.com](mailto:naman@oximy.com)

launches.tagline: AI-native observability platform for fast-moving engineering teams
launches.body:
# Sazabi - Datadog for the AI Era

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102391&key=user_uploads/282099/bc8014f4-5e17-4c76-be1c-3bd2b6ba26ec)

Sazabi is a next-generation observability platform designed for fast-moving, AI-native engineering teams. If you're using Datadog, Sentry, Grafana, or Axiom today, you could be moving ten times faster with Sazabi. **Book a demo [here](https://calendly.com/d/cyn6-s9f-tfq/meet-sazabi).**

### Rethinking Observability

Right now, every engineering team in the world is coming to the same conclusion: it doesn't matter how fast you can ship if your app is constantly going down. The antidote to production instability is observability, but not the flavor we have today. 

Legacy observability platforms can’t keep up with the pace of modern AI-driven software development. They take hours or days to set up. They are complex and clunky to use. The alerts they give you are noisy and confusing. They aren't built to be used with agents.

Sazabi is what Datadog would look like if it were built in 2026 instead of 2010:

* A simple chat-based user experience instead of endless dashboards. 
* Effortless agent-driven instrumentation that requires zero code or config changes. 
* Autonomous alerts that can contain all the relevant context and never misfire. 
*  A powerful CLI that gives your coding agent complete visibility into your observability data. 
*  Slack has the primary application entry point. 
* An AI agent that memorizes your codebase, architecture, traffic patterns, and past incidents.
* Native integrations with every major cloud provider and hosting service.
* A storage layer that uses AI for compression and is optimized specifically for agentic query patterns.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102391&key=user_uploads/282099/3e5d80bd-59bd-43b3-bc72-ae9edc68a2ed)

### How It Works

You can get started with Sazabi in less than 15 minutes. There are just three steps:

1. Connect your GitHub repository 
2. Install the Slack app 
3. Start sending logs

For legacy platforms, instrumentation is a headache. With Sazabi, it's effortless. We've got integrations with over 35 of the leading cloud hosting services, including Vercel, AWS, GCP, Temporal, Cloudflare, Neon, Supabase, and more. If we don't have a native integration, Sazabi can open a pull request with the necessary instrumentation changes. Our log intake is OpenTelemetry compatible.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102391&key=user_uploads/282099/563095d8-89fc-47cd-a4cf-94746d7540ff)

After setup, a few things happen automatically: 

* Sazabi scans your logs and codebase to learn more about the system, registering all key services, components, and product features to a live status page that gives you an overall view of system health.
* Sazabi's background agents begin monitoring your logs, codebase, and infrastructure for anomalies - everything from unfamiliar errors to traffic spikes to crash pods and failed deployments. 
* When an issue is detected, Sazabi sends you a rich Slack alert with all the relevant context, including the root cause.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102391&key=user_uploads/282099/f676f9dc-0af4-4c31-873f-abc1172484fe)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102391&key=user_uploads/282099/c81d2281-add8-4645-b873-524affd0d0ee)

You and anyone from your team can send Sazabi a follow-up message via Slack, CLI, Web, or MCP. Sazabi is great for ad hoc questions and queries too. Sazabi automations allow you to generate detailed reports at any cadence.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102391&key=user_uploads/282099/b8ab228d-23a7-40d2-960d-c469c6d25f19)

After receiving an alert, you can fix it directly with just a click of a button. Sazabi will open the pull request against your repo. If you prefer to use a different coding agent, it’s easy to hand off context -  Sazabi has integrations with Cursor, Codex, and Claude Code.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102391&key=user_uploads/282099/a95e8ecc-befb-4e31-a7a9-5523adea2548)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102391&key=user_uploads/282099/be62eeb2-a73f-431a-b99a-64823dc8fdc2)

Teams that use Sazabi are detecting issues they didn’t know they had and resolving incidents in minutes instead of hours.

### Logs Are All You Need

Sazabi is based on a few big ideas. The most important one: “logs are all you need”. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102391&key=user_uploads/282099/135568da-6b42-4f54-8e27-2e9d9d349f46)

What this means is that Sazabi doesn't require users to send metrics or traces. You only need to send us logs (stdout and stderr). Sazabi is able to answer complex queries, perform aggregations, profile endpoints, and trace requests through your entire system using just log data. The result is a much simpler instrumentation experience for you and your team, with all the power of a traditional observability platform.

### What Makes Us Different

A lot of companies are building in observability right now. How is Sazabi different?  Here’s how we think about the landscape:

*  **AI SRE startups like Traversal and Resolve.** These sit on top of third-party systems like Datadog. It's an approach that makes sense for enterprises that rely on legacy tools, but not the best solution. Sazabi has its own storage layer.
* **DIY solutions like Ramp’s “On-Call Assistant”.** It’s great to see so many companies building internal AI SREs. It proves demand, but it doesn't make sense for each company to build their own - especially when Sazabi is offering a better agent off-the-shelf.
* **Legacy players like Datadog, Grafana, Sentry, and Axiom.** You can try to use Claude Code with the Datadog MCP, and it will work OK, but not great.  importantly, this approach isn't stateful. Each investigation is completely new. Sazabi, on the other hand, accumulates memory and constantly gets better. More fundamentally, all of these companies predate AI agents and are structurally misaligned with AI.
* **LLM observability companies like Arize, Braintrust, LangChain, and Raindrop.** These are a narrow point solution for building and observing agents. Sazabi can do this too, but its scope is much broader than that. It's a general solution for observing any workload. We think that in the long-term there is no meaningful difference between observing agents and other types of software.

Sazabi's most important differentiator is our vertical integration. We're building every piece of the AI observability stack:

* The interfaces
* The agent
* The storage layer

The allows us to do things our competitors fundamentally can't, like analyze and memorize every historical incident, or optimize our DB for the specific query patterns of our agent. It's an Apple-style approach to observability. 

### Where We Are Today

Sazabi is currently in closed alpha, but we’re growing fast. In the past month we’ve onboarded 35 new teams, run 8,000 background investigations, detected 2,000 issues, ingested 2 TB of logs, and opened 200 PRs.  

Sazabi is founded by Sherwood Callaway, a two-time YC founder who previously started the infrastructure and observability teams at Brex. We’re a team of nine engineers in total, including three early members of the Brex team and two former observability founders. 

Our investors include angels from top AI dev tools and infrastructure startups. To name a few:

* Harrison Chase, CEO of LangChain
* Merrill Lutsky, founder and CEO of Graphite
* Ivan Burazin, founder and CEO of Daytona
* Matt Biilmann, founder and CEO of Netlify
* Paul Klein, founder and CEO of Browserbase

launches.body:
> **TLDR:** Create an API sandbox with the environments your CI, tests, and evals need. Your coding agent can start the API sandboxes (e.g Linear, Slack, Datadog), run tests, and inspect state changes. Ask your agent about archal.ai!

Hi everyone, I'm Aidan, the founder of Archal. I previously built agent environments at Scale AI and I've been an avid developer for most of my life, which led me to the problem Archal poses to solve.

[https:/youtu.be/pUfu1RFDYVk](https://youtu.be/pUfu1RFDYVk)

**What we found**

Coding agents are getting much better at writing integrations, but testing those integrations is still painful. Many providers do not offer a usable sandbox, so developers fall back to throwaway accounts, shared test workspaces, or thin mocks. Those options are difficult to reset and make it hard to know whether an agent actually completed a task or only returned a plausible response.

As Adam Bender at Google put it, “But with 10x more code and 10x more services, integration tests are going to become the most important part of your quality strategy.” (Google, Software engineering is at the tipping point)

**How Archal works**

With all of this in mind, I built Archal for a starting point of how the next generation of devs will do QA. It's a tool focused on giving agent developers and integration engineers API sandboxes of the SaaS platforms they use in prod pipelines. With Archal, a developer or their coding agent can start a sandbox, run the task, inspect what changed, and reset everything for the next test. We eliminate the need of separate test accounts, thin mocks and stubs, as well as overburdening rate limits on provider-owned sandboxes.

**Our ask**

We're giving out $20 in Archal credits to each new developer that signs up and starts a sandbox. We’d love for you to give it a try and give us feedback, cheers to making testing easier in the era of coding agents!

name: The Token Company
long_description:
Compression middleware that removes context bloat in milliseconds, lowering costs and improving end-to-end latency.

Compression is especially effective across natural language workloads. In a blind LLM arena case study with one of our customers, compressed requests increased user preference, lowered costs, and lifted purchase volume by 5%.
one_liner: Compression middleware that improves LLM outputs

question_answers.question: How did you decide to apply to Y Combinator? What was your experience applying, going through the batch, and fundraising at demo day?
question_answers.answer: I didn’t apply for the winter batch, but after the YC partners reached out and spoke with me, it seemed like the obvious choice. The batch has been awesome so far, and I’ve learned so much. Can’t wait for what’s to come :)

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Context bloat and inefficient LLM inputs. We preprocess inputs to remove useless tokens from the context, which results in faster, cheaper, and more accurate LLM answers.

Currently, this is not being done practically anywhere, which means billions of dollars and quadrillions of tokens are being wasted.

I decided to work on this because it is something much more fundamental than ordinary application layer companies, since it affects each one. And I like hard problems ;)

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
The vision is to optimize every LLM request in the world at the token level before it reaches a model.

Even if model labs dominate, there will still be multiple competing providers. We sit above them as a neutral efficiency layer, optimizing inputs across all models. Labs are incentivized to build bigger models and sell more tokens, not reduce usage across the ecosystem. As long as more than one lab exists, a cross-model optimization layer remains structurally defensible.

launches.title: The Token Company: Intelligent compression for LLM context bloat
launches.tagline: Intelligent compression for LLM context bloat
launches.body:
Hey everyone,I’m Otso Veisterä, founder of The Token Company (YC W26).

**TL;DR**\
We build LLM input compression using a fast machine learning model (not a generative LLM). It removes useless tokens from prompts via a drop-in API—cutting token counts, latency, and costs while improving model performance. It compresses 100k tokens in under 100ms.

<https://youtu.be/65ScMCGNPss>

**The Problem**\
Prompts bloat with redundant tokens from chat history, RAG docs, or large inputs. This wastes context windows, drives up costs, slows inference, and weakens model outputs. Heavy users face high bills and must limit context to stay affordable.

**The Solution**\
Our API compresses prompts intelligently, preserving semantic intent while stripping noise. Integration takes minutes.\
Benchmarks show accuracy gains (e.g., +2.7 percentage points on financial QA with up to 20% fewer tokens) and up to 37% faster end-to-end latency.

**My Ask**\
If you're running production LLMs and fighting context bloat, high costs, or latency, email me: [otso@thetokencompany.com](mailto:otso@thetokencompany.com)\
<https://thetokencompany.com>

launches.body:
We’re Mohammad and Pranav (Moda, W26). **We built monitoring & reliability for AI agents.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98435&key=user_uploads/2168306/84330bae-242e-447d-a656-800061f4b1ac)

**In production, AI agents fail silently all the time:** tool calls that error or time out, agents that claim they “did it” without actually doing it, prompt injections that cause data leakage, and long customer chats that hide the real issue. Most teams only find out after users complain, churn, or something breaks.

<https://youtu.be/aKPDhL_AE4E>

### **The problem:**

When an agent fails, the “bug” is rarely one line of code. It might be a flaky tool, a prompt regression, a bad retrieval result, or a jailbreak attempt.

But most teams still debug agents by skimming transcripts, grepping logs, and hoping they notice the real issue. Previous tools were built for clicks, not for long, messy conversations with skills, MCP’s and tools.

As agents get more autonomous, this gets worse. Small changes in prompts, tools, or integrations can cause big reliability and security problems at scale.

### **What we built:**

Moda is monitoring & reliability for AI agents. It turns conversations and tool traces into low-noise, actionable signals.

**Trace-first drilldowns:** click from a metric or alert straight into the exact messages and tool calls that caused it.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98435&key=user_uploads/2168306/6e062a13-340e-452f-9676-2bdd790d94e4)

**Conversation segmentation:** automatically splits long chats into topic segments so you can debug the right unit of work.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98435&key=user_uploads/2168306/90151d61-e51b-45da-ac29-72af5c8a31d6)

**Failure detection:** flags tool-call errors, timeouts, and “claimed it worked” runs.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98435&key=user_uploads/2168306/335d8a83-6301-4d0e-af31-a75778cbbb0e)

**Quality & safety signals:** highlights hallucinations, user frustration, and prompt injection attempts.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98435&key=user_uploads/2168306/7ee4b5f6-ddc0-47a3-9e9c-3538f6764acc)

\
**Regression tracking:** measure the impact of prompt and harness changes, and catch regressions before customers do.\
\
Want to see Moda on your agent in production? Book a quick call: [https://moda.dev](https://moda.dev)

### **About Us:**

**Mohammad** built AI agents and infrastructure at **Shopify, Notion, and Clio**, shipping systems that scaled agents to real users.

**Pranav** built data infrastructure at banks and insurance firms before diving into building AI agents at **Shopify** and **Cerebral Valley**

We both dropped out of University of Waterloo to solve what we believe to be the biggest problem in the next 10 years, AI systems are unreliable, Moda is going to solve that.

Visit us at [https://moda.dev](https://moda.dev) | [pranav@modaflows.com](mailto:pranav@modaflows.com)

Shofo is building the largest index of videos.

<https://youtu.be/C0c3Q3MsRUg>

### **❌ The Problem**

AI labs require massive, high-quality video data to train multimodal models, but clean, custom video datasets cost millions and take months to collect.

### **✅ Our Solution**

We're building the world's largest library of videos by combining public videos collected from the open web and private videos aggregated from thousands of different sources. Both feed into a single, continuously updating index of billions of videos that we clean, search, and label to build custom datasets for AI teams.

**Ask;** If you or someone you know runs physical operations (manufacturing, logistics, retail, security) and wants to automate visual tasks without buying new hardware, we’d love to connect!

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=36OaIJ4FPZ8>

* [Andrey Gizdov](https://www.linkedin.com/in/andreygizdov/), CEO, dropped a fully-funded **PhD** scholarship from Fulbright, worth **$170,000**, with invitations at **Harvard and MIT**, where he worked on real-time vision models.

For physical operations, the best technology available to catch these events in real-time has been a human staring at a monitor.

**Solution:**

OpenVector is an AI that brings action to any camera.

* **Plain English to AI Model:** No coding or expensive setup. Simply describe your task in plain English, and OpenVector automatically builds the best AI vision model for it, and watches your camera feeds 24/7. It’s an app that takes 2 minutes to download and set up, and works with any camera.
* **Acts Like a Human:** OpenVector operates a computer just like a human based on what it sees.
* **Legacy Integration:** It automatically integrates with your existing systems to make a call, send an email, update your POS or CRM, or trigger a webhook the second an event happens.
* **Zero New Hardware:** Works entirely with the cameras you already have installed (custom end-to-end solutions also available).

**We’ve Already Started:**

OpenVector is already live and seeing use cases across security, retail, manufacturing, and logistics. We are tracking production cycle efficiency directly from existing CCTV, ensuring good-manufacturing-practices, and catching physical design errors.

**Now Onboarding:**

Every lab now wins or loses on its edge cases, and edge cases need specific data captured by specific people: data that doesn't exist anywhere online. Whoever can go collect the right data first ships the better model first. Human labor is half of global GDP, and almost none of it has been recorded yet.

**What Hub does**

We capture this data through a global network of humans, across all continents. We route and activate the exact people who fit a lab's brief and deliver in days, not the months it takes to source a generic dataset off the shelf. Because we collect the data ourselves, we can attest its provenance, which you can't do for data you didn't capture. Our ML and QA pipelines then verify and enrich it, so we meet the hardest dataset requirements labs throw at us. The moat isn't the data, it's how fast we can go get it.

**Traction**

From 5-figure to 7-figure in revenue agreement on successful data delivery. We now work with some of the biggest frontier AI labs and robotics companies in the world.

**The ask**

Two asks: —> You're building frontier models or robots and data is your constraint. \
—> You're a top robotics engineer, a PhD whose research touches robotics or egocentric data, or someone with deep experience at a leading robotics lab, we're hiring. \

launches.title: Limrun - Your cloud agent can build mobile apps now
launches.tagline: Extend your cloud agent with XCode, Android and more
launches.body:
TLDR; We provide remote XCode, iOS & Android Simulators and more to extend cloud agents’ capabilities. Replit, Rork, Momentic AI, x1 and many others built on our cloud and now we open it up to all mobile dev teams so you can use your favorite cloud agent for iOS and Android apps too.

If you have a mobile app, let’s talk! <https://cal.com/team/limrun/mobile-app-dev-in-cloud>

<https://youtu.be/fYkRpsyPLkQ>

---

When code is written by humans, it lives on our laptops and PCs, but that's changing now that teams of agents are writing code alongside us. Today, code written by agents is moving to the cloud: Cursor Cloud, Devin AI, Codex Web, in-house solutions with sandboxes and more.

Now the problem is that all these cloud agents have Linux-based sandboxes as opposed to our laptops that we bought specifically for coding. If you want to use sandboxes for iOS development, you don’t have XCode. If you have an Android app, no emulator that works well. There’s no properly priced GPU option for running Unity either.

Limrun is building a cloud that provides these apps as remote services running in the environments they were designed to while letting your agents use them remotely from your favorite sandbox. All you need is a single skill file to teach your agent how to use our remote services. That’s it. No change of sandbox or agent.

Today, we provide 3 services:

* XCode: With a single CLI call, your code is synced, a build is triggered and your agent gets the logs to iterate.
* iOS Simulator: Your agent can request a simulator to test the app with built-in AX tree or your favorite framework like Appium/Maestro/Detox etc.
* Android Emulator: Similarly, it can request an emulator that will be proxied via an “adb” tunnel so it’s as if locally running.

These are not full sandboxes. We provide the highest level interface so your agent can orchestrate what it needs remotely and we optimize the heck out of the rest; hardware encoders for streaming, warm NVMe caches for building, below 1s boot times, on-demand recording, asset storage and more.

Here is an example flow where Cursor Cloud (or an agent in E2B/Daytona/Docker etc) builds an iOS game in Swift:

* Agent takes the issue from Linear and spins up its sandbox.
* Writes the Swift code and calls the “lim xcode build .” command, streaming logs back.
* Iterates over compiler errors.
* Requests an iOS simulator with “lim ios create” and attaches it.
* Plays the game with batch actions that provide millisecond precision.
* We return the recording that it reviews, sees the bugs, implements the fixes.
* Finally, records a demo video and constructs a preview link to drop on the PR.

It goes from Linear issue to a fully tested PR with demo and preview link that opens in the browser with realtime streaming or you can install to your device over WebUSB without downloading anything.

If you have a mobile app, let’s talk\![ https://cal.com/team/limrun/mobile-app-dev-in-cloud](https://cal.com/team/limrun/mobile-app-dev-in-cloud)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99878&key=user_uploads/1618136/2310c230-6719-4913-ba16-43c8cab6c2d9)

**tldr:** LLMs are built for human-in-the-loop tasks which are highly non-deterministic in nature. We built an AI model for tasks that require high accuracy and verifiable data you can build workflows around.

Interfaze is an AI model built on a new architecture that combines specialized DNN+CNN models with transformers for developer tasks that require deterministic output and high consistency like:

* Vision (OCR, Object detection, GUI) 
* Structured web extraction
* Audio (STT, Diarization, Audio semantics)
* Classification (Image, Text)
* Web search and more

**Try here:** <https://interfaze.ai>

If you’ve ever tried to build a production application using LLMs for tasks like OCR, web scraping, or strict structured data extraction, you already know the pain: hallucinated keys, broken JSON, hidden inaccurate data and massive latency spikes.

You usually end up chaining multiple open source models together just to get a reliable result but face challenges with scaling or being stuck with outdated models from providers like AWS, Azure and GCP.

**Model comparison**

launches.body:
Hey YC!! Faiz and Saheed here from Minicor ([minicor.com](http://minicor.com))

**TLDR;** AI companies selling into healthcare, automotive, financial services, and logistics can't go live because their customers run on legacy desktop software with no APIs. The only way in is clicking through the UI, and it breaks constantly. Minicor is a platform for building self-healing desktop automation that scales.

Launch video:\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nzH4ekkaA2c>

**The problem**

Our customers selling into legacy industries can't go live because the systems of record their customers use (EHRs, ERPs, DMS) are Windows desktop apps with no APIs. The only way to read / write is through UI automations, but desktop RPA at scale breaks constantly. Even small error rates become hundreds of failures a day, and every one needs manual intervention.

They're signing customers but don't have capacity to integrate because they're too busy fighting fires with existing RPAs; or their prospects are blocked because they need "proof" they can write back to their systems, and spinning up a desktop automation POC takes too long.

**In production**

We're live right now processing thousands of workflows a week across healthcare EHRs and other legacy systems. Our agents write AI-generated data into desktop apps in real-time. We went live with a customer in 3 weeks post POC.

**How it works**

1. Install our Desktop Client on the machines running the legacy software.
2. Speak the automation into existence - either through your favourite coding agent via our MCP, or to us directly. You get an API endpoint to trigger it.
3. Minicor handles everything after that. Only pay when the data gets in

**Demos**

Generating an automation with our MCP:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99004&key=user_uploads/1037983/3566b35e-8721-428e-9c8c-99b2d4f337a4)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99004&key=user_uploads/1037983/ce87bffc-0860-43ab-a1b9-94d5b5656adf)

**About us**

Saheed and I both started our careers building bespoke / legacy system integrations. Me at a YC startup, Saheed at Morgan Stanley and Ford. We met in 2019 in a UX class, built a non-profit together over the pandemic, and started working on this in 2023.

We started with an observability and error recovery platform for API integrations, and got pulled into Desktop automations when a prospect closed hyper quickly on the promise that we could help them connect to an on-prem EMR.

launches.body:
### Credentials

We’ve spent years working together building large scale distributed systems that run on hundreds of thousands of machines and serve billions of users. **Every time you leverage your network for a warm intro on LinkedIn, you use three databases that we’ve built: [Venice](https://venicedb.org/),[ Liquid](https://www.linkedin.com/blog/engineering/graph-systems/liquid-the-soul-of-a-new-graph-database-part-1), and[ Espresso](https://engineering.linkedin.com/teams/data/data-infrastructure/storage-infra/espresso).**

After LinkedIn, **we were tech-leads of [Ray](https://github.com/ray-project/ray)**, the leading open-source compute platform used by companies such as xAI, Cursor, Bridgewater, P72, Man Group, Two Sigma, and others. Ray has [\~12M](https://pypistats.org/packages/ray) weekly downloads and is part of the PyTorch Foundation.

### Product

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C6tl8Fr8t2I>

We’re building large scale high performance computing (HPC) clusters for **quantitative trading firms** to run **parallel simulation workloads such as backtesting.** 

The scale we’re targeting is

* 100 to 50,000 nodes of mixed hardware (CPUs and GPUs) on hyperscalers and neoclouds.
* up to 5,000,000 parallel tasks.
* spot instances for cheaper compute across multiple availability zones, hyperscalers, and neoclouds.
* < 50ms overhead for task dispatch and scheduling.
* run the compute in your cloud or on-prem environment to keep your alpha secure.

Our goal is to **make testing trading strategies fast, cheap, and reliable.** 

### Vision

We know that existing solutions do not handle this scale, do not have first-class support for spot-instances, and will not match our low-latency and high throughput performance. 

Our technology generalizes to other large-scale compute workloads such as

1. **post-training and reinforcement learning (RL)** for frontier and applied AI labs
2. **massively parallel robotics simulation and sim-to-real training** for robot foundation model teams
3. **virtual screening and molecular dynamics** for techbio and pharma R&D
4. **scientific simulation** (CFD, climate, seismic, FEA) for HPC teams looking to move beyond MPI and SLURM.

### Ask

Reach out if you

1. Are running simulation workloads that require lots of computation at a quant trading firm.
2. If you need HPC for a different use-case.
3. Want to grab a beer and talk about distributed systems or HPC.

Cheers!

Ibrahim and Zac

launches.body:
Website: <https://www.watolabs.com>

**TL;DR: Wato is a shared AI workspace for teams.** It helps companies keep their AI workflows, company knowledge, integrations, agent sessions, and agent-generated work inside the organization instead of scattered across individual chats, local files, or personal AI accounts. All of this is done via one, unified MCP.

**Ask:** If your team is using AI agents for engineering, ops, sales, research, finance, support, or internal workflows, we’d love to see how we can help. We’re especially interested in teams setting up MCP/tools, sharing prompts or workflows internally, launching cloud agents, or trying to preserve useful agent context across the company.

**The problem:** Teams are already using AI for real company workflows: debugging production issues, preparing sales calls, analyzing customer data, updating models, drafting client deliverables, and searching across internal systems.

But the work usually disappears into individual tools and accounts. The context, prompts, decisions, files, and tool setups that made the output useful are hard for the next teammate to find, trust, or reuse.

**What Wato does:** Wato gives each team a shared, permissioned AI workspace.

Teams can connect approved integrations and MCP tools, build shared memory, publish reusable skills, run collaborative cloud agent sessions, host live artifacts and dashboards, and trace tool calls across the organization.

The goal is simple: **when one person or agent learns something useful, builds a workflow, or creates an artifact, that knowledge should stay with the company and become available to the right people.**

**What’s included:**

\- **Team memory** for durable company knowledge agents can reuse

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102479&key=user_uploads/3203486/64ae52b1-6599-49c7-9e99-297e4e71a9ae)

\- **Approved MCP tools and integrations** with org, team, per-user, and tool-level permissions

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102479&key=user_uploads/3203486/e8673b85-1e38-456a-ad60-d5d90ed2fe80)

\- **Reusable skills and workflows** library so teams don’t prompt from scratch every time

\- **Cloud agent sessions** that teammates can view, continue, and collaborate on, with access to a desktop, computer use, filesystem, and environment set up.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102479&key=user_uploads/3203486/b3da2993-c84f-4347-ad8a-46fea54ee809)

\- **Automations** that can be created from connector triggers or run on a specific cadence.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102479&key=user_uploads/3203486/edc32ad1-ae2e-42ef-9014-0782e8112464)

\- **Live artifacts and dashboards** that can use approved company data

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102479&key=user_uploads/3203486/700f9d35-6150-4012-b58c-e56b54b39c30)

\- **Tool-call tracing and audit logs** so teams can see what agents accessed and produced

Wato also works with the AI tools teams already use, including Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code, and other MCP-compatible environments. You add the Wato MCP once, authenticate with your company account, and your agent gets access to the right team memory, skills, and approved tools.

**Backstory:** We started working on Wato after seeing the same problem across institutions adopting these tools like Claude or Codex. A super user would figure out a great workflow, debugging process, research method, client-prep flow, or tool setup, but the useful part would end up stuck in a chat thread, local file, or personal account. Then the next person would start over.

At the same time, companies didn’t want every employee independently managing MCP configs, tool permissions, prompts, and scattered agent instructions. They needed a shared layer between the company and the AI tools its people use to normalize AI use.

That became Wato.

**We’d love to talk to teams who are:**

\- **using agents** across engineering, ops, sales, research, finance, support, or internal workflows

\- setting up **MCP servers or internal tools** for agent use

\- trying to **share prompts, skills, playbooks, or workflows** across a team

\- creating AI-generated **dashboards**, docs, reports, or **artifacts** that need to be shared securely

\- worried about **company knowledge** disappearing into personal AI accounts

\- thinking about **permissions**, **review**, **tracing**, or **governance** for agent work

If this sounds familiar, and I’m guessing it does for a lot of you, we’d love to show you Wato and get feedback.

launches.title: Ardent - Clone any postgres DB of any size in <6s
launches.tagline: Ardent lets engineers give their coding agents 1:1 clones of prod to test code and prevent downtime
launches.body:
Hi! I’m Vikram founder of [@Ardent](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/31475). **We let you clone any postgres DB in <6s** so your coding agents and devs can test code on a 1:1 of production or dev DBs with zero risk

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=100815&key=user_uploads/1239054/b0ebde7f-0ac7-49a9-8f42-e4fb3f26d585)

We’re working with companies with huge amounts of data like Supermemory and YC companies like [@Surface Labs](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/28921)

**This is me cloning a 1.6TB db is 6s:**

<https://youtu.be/8Q4IX7HUJmo>

Website: <https://tryardent.com/>

**How did we get here (the problem)?**

Ardent was a reaction to the failure of our last product - an AI Data Engineer. It was a coding agent that generated data pipelines, wrote migrations, backfills and other things you’d expect of a data engineer.

While the code _looked_ great we had no way of testing generated code. Writing to prod was out of the question and dev environments were never in sync, shared amongst devs which caused write clashes between agents, and was a huge pain to manage. **_What we needed was a ephemeral DB sandbox per agent of the user’s DB._**

Because of how hard testing was, generated code would never be tested and was too unstable to put in production. Database failures almost always mean downtime, a risk both we and customers were obviously not willing to take. We churned almost 200K in ARR

This problem exists with any coding agent today. We’re shipping 100x more DB code to production and we mostly just hope to god it works the same as dev.

**Ardent - Isolated <6s database clones that let you test agent code:**

Ardent solves the DB sandbox problem by letting you create 6s clones of ANY postgres DB regardless of size, allowing you to give every developer and every agent a full copy of production or dev to test against.

Clones autoscale to zero when not in use, use copy on write for massive storage efficiency and can be loaded with a single CLI command (zero infra management)

You can see the exact results of any code run against the DB in a perfect 1:1 reproduction and don’t have to change your DB provider.

The entire thing runs as a CLI that feels exactly like git. Cloning is as simple as “ardent branch create <name>”

This means you can spin up instant environments to test _every_ line of DB code with none of the overhead

**Asks**

**Use Ardent at your company to go faster by let agents work safely at the DB layer and prevent regressions:** <https://cal.com/vikram-chennai/yc-reserved>

**Introduce me to series A-C engineering leaders (Founders, CTOs, VP of Eng):** Many of the later stage startups we’ve talked to have the majority of their engineers shipping with claude, codex or cursor on migrations, backfills and pretty much any code that hits the DB. They will eventually crash their production DB unless they’re rigorously testing. I’d like to prevent those crashes :)

Contact me: [vikram@tryardent.com](mailto:vikram@tryardent.com)

launches.title: Infinity — A New Computation Layer
launches.tagline: Months of work, done in days. Every app gets its own GPU, in one browser tab.
launches.body:
Hey YC 👋

We're Rounak, Bishal & Sourya — co-founders of ProjectX (P26). Today we're launching Infinity.

\[<https://youtu.be/ZYf2vdWMkDk>\]

### TL;DR

**Infinity is a new computation layer — a web-based OS where every app you open runs on its own independent compute and GPU, inside one shared workspace.** Open Blender, Unreal, Isaac Sim, DaVinci, VS Code in the same browser tab. Each app is its own machine with its own GPU. They share one filesystem and one terminal. Windows and Linux apps run side by side. Runs on any browser, on any device. Open fifty apps at once — nothing slows down.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102024&key=user_uploads/2936820/28491e87-8d68-4bd0-b0ea-860d2d7d1825)

### Problem

The apps people actually use to build the future — Blender, Unreal, Isaac Sim, Houdini, the CAD/CAM/CAE stack, ML pipelines — still need a $5K workstation under your desk. The cloud was supposed to fix this and didn't. Renting a cloud GPU means hours of driver installs, version matching, container debugging before you do any actual work. Streamed desktops (Citrix, Paperspace, Shadow) give you one VM with one GPU — built for one user running one app at a time. Open Blender and Unreal at the same time and you're fighting yourself for resources.

It's hitting agents too. Claude Cowork runs on your laptop, sharing your GPU with everything else. Manus runs in a CPU-bound microVM that can't open heavy apps at all. Claude can drive Blender via MCP, but Blender still runs on your machine — the agent just borrows your compute.

### Solution

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102024&key=user_uploads/2936820/281d546a-52f7-4932-b92e-30608f83f249)

Infinity makes every app its own computer.

Open Blender, you get a machine with a dedicated GPU. Open Unreal in the next window, that's a second machine with its own GPU. Open Isaac Sim, that's a third. They share a filesystem and a terminal so the workspace feels like one computer, but underneath they're independent machines. Open fifty apps, you have fifty machines. Nothing slows down. Runs entirely in a browser tab — Chromebook, iPad, five-year-old laptop, doesn't matter.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102024&key=user_uploads/2936820/971299ab-663b-4181-ae7e-64ed286ecda2)

\
Every Infinity workspace comes will soon ship with a built-in computer use agent that can access run applications without being constrained by compute, no matter how many applications you run or how heavy the workflow is. Tell it what you want, and it spins up the apps, drives them, hands files between them, and finishes the work. You can drive Infinity with a mouse and keyboard, or you can drive it with a prompt.

A concrete example. You prompt: _"Make a 90-second product launch video. Write the script, generate the voiceover, edit in DaVinci, render the 3D logo in Blender, post to YouTube."_

Six apps spin up at once:

* Claude writes the script
* ElevenLabs generates the voiceover
* DaVinci Resolve edits the cut
* Blender renders the 3D logo
* Chrome uploads to YouTube
* VS Code writes the publish script

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102024&key=user_uploads/2936820/fc66db17-d35b-4f3d-8459-cec58a4cebc2)

They share a workspace. They hand files to each other. **One finished video in an hour, not three days.**

### Where we are — 15 days in early preview 

* **20,000+ builders** signed up
* **1,160% growth** in the last 14 days
* **20M+ impressions** on X and Instagram
* **10,000+ signups** in the last 7 days
* **Out of server capacity** — rate-limiting new signups while we scale

Used by engineers at **Reliance Industries, CEMEX, Cognizant, Globant, Ola Electric, Lattice, Quizizz, Appsmith, Bonsai Robotics, Induction Labs, Basis Robotics**, and 130+ more teams. All inbound. Our first public demo crashed our servers at midnight; we scaled the infra live at 3am and woke up to inbound from 50+ enterprises.

### Future

Once every app has its own compute, agents stop being a separate problem.

A computer-use agent is just another app — except the agent drives itself. Because every agent gets its own machine on Infinity, ten agents work in parallel without stepping on each other. The thing that's impossible today — ten parallel cursors, ten parallel renders, ten parallel models — is the default on Infinity.

We're shipping the multi-agent runtime next. One prompt, a mother agent plans and coordinates, child agents execute on dedicated hardware — each routing through Claude, GPT, Gemini, or any MCP tool. Same substrate humans use, given to agents.

### Ask

If you are, or know any of the following, we want to hear from you:

**Heavy-GPU teams.** Robotics, Physical AI, 3D/VFX, ML, post-production, CAD/CAM/CAE. If you're buying workstations or wrestling with cloud GPU setup, let's talk.

**Agent builders.** If you're shipping a computer-use agent and hitting the "where does this actually run" wall, we should talk early.

Free Infinity credits for all YC founders and alums. Email me directly: [rounak@projectx.cloud](mailto:rounak@projectx.cloud)

— Rounak, Bishal & Sourya

launches.title: Expanse - Unlock wasted GPU capacity
launches.tagline: Unlock wasted GPU capacity.
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Expanse unlocks wasted GPU capacity. We’re the intelligence layer for compute infrastructure. Submit jobs with the right resources. Optimise them to run faster. Debug failures in seconds, not days. Works on cloud and on-prem HPC.

Want to know how much more you can get out of your hardware? Schedule a call: <https://book.getexpanse.io>

**Problem**

Running compute on a cluster means guessing memory, time, and GPUs before you submit. Get it wrong and your job fails mid-run. Over-guess and you pay for compute you never use. 30% of cloud spend is lost to over-allocation \[1\]. Microsoft Research found their own deep learning jobs hit 50% GPU utilisation or lower \[2\].

Sizing jobs takes decades of experience. Memory patterns, batching, GPU threading, CPU vectorisation. AI agents don’t have enough information to fix it either. SLURM and Kubernetes don’t expose enough structured data. Even strong platform teams are forced to choose: spend time debugging and optimising every job, or accept the waste. AI infrastructure spending will hit $2.52 trillion in 2026 \[3\]. The waste grows with every new cluster. This problem isn’t going away.

**Solution**

Expanse learns your cluster. We analyse your code and hardware telemetry, then track them over time. Our deep learning models build a picture of what your workloads actually need. Predictions get sharper with every job.

Our models are deployed on your cluster. All analysis runs on your network. Your code and telemetry never leave your infrastructure. We can’t see your data, and you maintain full data sovereignty.

One command installs Expanse on your cluster. You get two tools.

`expanse analyse` - for every job:

* **Suggests the right resource configuration**
* **Predicts failures from historical code and telemetry patterns**
* **Surfaces code-level optimisations that increase efficiency**

`expanse diagnose` - for every failure:

* **Finds the root cause**
* **Returns solution-oriented logs with the exact code and config changes to fix it**

Days of debugging and optimising become seconds. Platform teams get what they need to do this in minutes instead of weeks.

**Founders**

We're four engineers from the University of Edinburgh, all coming from top quant funds and national supercomputing centres. Ismaeel built the first multimodal HPC resource predictor at EPCC (Edinburgh's Parallel Computing Centre), beating every published baseline. Yafet built the first GNN cluster graph network for predicting SLURM queue wait times. Eren built decentralised foundation model training systems at Edinburgh. Niko trained large-scale speech ML models on GPU clusters and architected cloud and Kubernetes infrastructure at one of the largest hedge funds in the world. We left our jobs to fix this ourselves.

**CTA / Ask**

Running compute and not getting enough out of what you’re paying for? Failing jobs, unclear errors, bills too high? We’d love to chat.

Know anyone in AI infrastructure (managing cloud and/or on-premise data centres), quant finance, drug discovery, or AI research labs? An intro would mean a lot :)

**YC Deal**

All YC companies running serious ML training can contact us for a discounted pilot. We’ll find inefficiencies and wastage on your compute setup. Then we deploy Expanse, no changes to your workflows. You get more out of the hardware you’re paying for.

Reach out: [founders@expanse.sh](mailto:founders@expanse.sh) or <https://book.getexpanse.io>

References

\[1\] <https://grafana.com/blog/2023/03/03/how-to-optimize-resource-utilization-with-kubernetes-monitoring-for-grafana-cloud>

\[2\] <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/an-empirical-study-on-low-gpu-utilization-of-deep-learning-jobs/>

\[3\] <https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-1-15-gartner-says-worldwide-ai-spending-will-total-2-point-5-trillion-dollars-in-2026>

AI agents are becoming incredibly capable online, but the moment you need one to make a phone call or send a text, everything falls apart. You end up stitching together telecom providers, voice infrastructure, compliance, routing, and your own memory layer. Giving an agent a phone number should be simple. It wasn't.

So we built [AgentPhone](http://agentphone.ai/): the telephony infrastructure layer for AI agents.\
\
<https://youtu.be/Gsj_BaaCDD4>

### **TL;DR:**

* One API to give any AI agent its own phone number
* iMessage, WhatsApp, RCS, SMS, Calling, and more soon
* A trusted identity so agents can reach people and businesses in the real world

### **Who's Using It**

Teams at Google's Agent Development Kit, Replit, Y Combinator, Sim AI, LangChain, and Alchemy are already building with AgentPhone.

### **The Problem**

The $2T global telecom industry was built for humans. AI agents today can browse the web, write code, and manage entire workflows. But they still can't pick up the phone. A lot of business still runs on calls and texts, channels that existed before the internet and email. If agents are going to do real work, they need to work on the channels people already use.

### **How It Works**

AgentPhone gives developers a single API to provision phone numbers for their agents with voice and messaging built in and no compliance headaches. Just plug in and your agent can talk and text to the world.

### **Things already built on AgentPhone:**

* An AI talent recruiter that messages and screens candidates
* AI employees with their own phone numbers that handle workflows end to end
* Our own company brain that Manav and Meet use internally to run AgentPhone

### **About Us**

We're [Meet](https://www.linkedin.com/in/meetmodi-/) and [Manav](https://www.linkedin.com/in/manav2modi). We met 21 years ago when our mom gave birth to Meet. We've been building together ever since.

launches.body:
Software development is becoming much more parallel. Coding agents let a team have dozens or hundreds of related changes moving at the same time, creating more branches, reviews, CI runs, and automation than existing workflows were designed to absorb.

Today, we’re opening GitCafe in public beta. It is a Git forge built for teams where humans and coding agents may ship hundreds or thousands of changes a day. We’re building the hosting, review, CI, security, and automation layer for that way of working.\
\
Hundreds of users are already on GitCafe, and we’re currently running trials with roughly a dozen YC companies.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109445&key=user_uploads/1920545/eecbfb4f-82f1-4660-8ee8-aeea5273a8b9)

Generating code is only part of the problem. Teams still need to understand what is changing, review it safely, keep CI moving, catch security issues, and coordinate work without becoming overwhelmed.

We’re not building GitCafe because putting repositories, code review, and CI in one product is new. We’re building it because we believe the workload those systems need to support is about to change dramatically.

We started by rebuilding the Git infrastructure itself. Now we’re closing the product gap feature by feature.

Recently, we added secret scanning, Buildkite and Harmont CI support, stacked diffs with Jujutsu and Sapling integration, and beta support for GitHub Actions.

These are foundational capabilities, not the destination. Building them on infrastructure we own gives us a base we can keep extending for higher-volume, agent driven development.

The honest version is that GitCafe is behind GitHub today. GitHub has spent more than a decade building an enormous product, and GitCafe does not yet have every workflow, administrative control, or integration that mature teams need. Some features are missing, some are experimental, and some edges are rough. We expect to earn the broader product surface, not claim it on day one.

We’re opening GitCafe now because the fastest way to improve it is to put it in the hands of teams doing real work.

If your team is already using coding agents heavily, try GitCafe at <https://git.cafe> and tell us where the workflow breaks down.\
\

launches.body:
We train human brain cells for compute. In March, we trained them to play Doom; now we got them to do next-token prediction.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109992&key=user_uploads/3388159/cbefdb79-ad5b-4e03-ae35-d2a482a05351)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109992&key=user_uploads/3388159/ce53a90f-7180-4eab-b23e-d770a5e375a7)

**The Problem**

Modern models require enormous amounts of energy and training data, while still struggling with continual learning and adapting efficiently to new tasks. Biological brains solve these problems very differently. They learn continuously, adapt from limited experience, and operate on roughly the power of a light bulb.\
\
**Solution**

Parasma is developing the algorithms and infrastructure needed to turn human brain cells into useful compute. The human brain is the most capable and energy-efficient learning system we know. Our goal is to reliably train biological substrates and use them for general computation, robotics, and eventually direct biological training. In March, we trained human brain cells to play Doom, which got hundreds of millions of views across social media. Since then, we’ve been working toward more general tasks. Most recently, we got the cells to perform token prediction: given a sequence of tokens converted to electrical stimuli, the neurons learn to predict what comes next with no GPU.

Long-term, biological compute will offer orders-of-magnitude improvements in energy and sample efficiency, while enabling native continual learning.

**Team**

I previously worked on neuromorphic computing and reinforcement learning during my master’s.

Before that, I built a successful digital-item marketplace with > $1.7M of listed goods and played games professionally.\
\
Check out our press release here:\
<https://parasma.com/news/human-brain-cells-do-next-token-prediction>

name: Orchestra
long_description:
Orchestra is an inference cloud. We capture your AI work traces, train smaller models, and automatically deploy them (only when they outperform the expensive model you are currently paying for).

Instead of renting the same frontier model forever, your AI infrastructure gets faster, smarter, and cheaper every time it runs.

Suppose your product uses Claude for a repetitive legal workflow.

Orchestra observes successful production runs, learns the specific tools and judgment required for that workflow, and trains a specialized open-weight model.

Once that model matches or beats Claude on a held-out evaluation, Orchestra starts routing production traffic to it.

As more work is completed, the model keeps improving.

We started Orchestra because we believe every company using AI should be accumulating intelligence, not accumulating API bills.
